en: The Philippine eagle is the largest and heaviest known eagle, with a specialized facial disc of stiff feathers that enhances its hearing to hunt in dense forests.
Dr. Fe del Mundo invented a makeshift bamboo incubator for premature babies that uses hot water bottles to regulate temperature without needing electricity.
The Katipunan's official newspaper, Kalayaan, originally printed only 2,000 copies using a manually operated wooden printing press hidden in a Binondo house.
The Philippine Declaration of Independence was proclaimed on June 12, 1898, but the country did not gain full international recognition until July 4, 1946.
The Ifugao people built the Banaue Rice Terraces over 2,000 years ago using only hands and simple tools, creating an irrigation system that still functions today.
Before the Spanish arrived, many Filipinos wrote on bamboo and leaves using Baybayin, an ancient alphabet where vowels are inherent in every consonant.
The Waling-waling orchid requires a specific symbiotic fungus in its native high-altitude cloud forests just to germinate its tiny, dust-like seeds.
While exiled in Dapitan, Jose Rizal discovered three new animal species for science, including a rare flying lizard now named Draco rizali.
The MassKara Festival in Bacolod originally started in 1980 to lift the city's spirits during a severe economic crisis and a tragic ferry sinking.
The Pearl of Lao Tzu, found in Palawan, is one of the world's largest natural pearls, weighing over 14 pounds and measuring 9 inches wide.
The Philippine Senate is composed of 24 senators who are elected nationwide at-large, meaning every voter across the entire country votes for the same candidates.
The tradition of Bayanihan originally involved an entire community physically lifting and relocating a traditional nipa hut by carrying its bamboo poles together.
